proof_nl: Let n be an integer with n > 1, and let t be a real number with 0 <= t < 1. Since n > 1, in particular n > 0. Multiplying the inequalities 0 <= t < 1 by the positive number n preserves their directions, giving 0 <= nt < n. This is exactly the desired conclusion.
solver_summary: Because n is positive, multiplying 0 <= t < 1 by n yields 0 <= nt < n.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly derives 0 <= n*t < n from 0 <= t < 1 and n > 1 by multiplying by the positive integer n. It matches the lemma statement exactly and uses no illegitimate dependencies.
